title: dev-harden harden.json, one recurring correction, placed as the cheapest check that can catch it
description: The output of the dev-harden skill, written to <evid_root>/harden/<fingerprint>/harden.json. One artifact per correction. The skill walks the fix ladder top down (structure, static, verification, prose) and records why every higher band was skipped, so a prose rule can never be written while a check that fails was possible. validate.py enforces this as DEV-HARDEN-L1 (a reason for every higher band; status tied to band and evidence). Consumers branch on `status`. A rule only reaches the gate when a human runs rule_probe.py --apply --by, which flips status to rule-applied and fills `applied`. v1.1.0 (additive): review misses are a third input. A prod-regressed run, or a reviewer-eval case the reviewer missed or only partly caught, arrives through the harden queue with source `review-miss` and a `miss` block (origin, ref, the review verdict, the uncaught locations, the mechanical facts of what the reviewer had). validate.py enforces DEV-HARDEN-M1: `review-miss` in correction.sources and a `miss` object go together; unless status is blocked, `miss.lacked` must name a kind (check, context, expectation, instruction, nothing) and a non-blank statement of what the reviewer did not have in front of it; kind `nothing` must end declined (or blocked); and declining a miss that did lack something needs a decline_reason. Older artifacts (no `miss`, no `review-miss` source) validate unchanged.

status.description: rule-proposed = a conventions rule passed rule_probe.py and waits for a human --apply; rule-applied = a human applied it, the gate enforces it from the next run; ticket-drafted = the fix belongs in the target repo (an API or architecture change, or a linter rule plus removing the existing copies) and a ticket was drafted for a loop, never filed or coded here; expectation-proposed = only running the app can prove it, an expectation was proposed (a human blesses it via human-explore); guideline-proposed = no higher band can catch it, a guidelines paragraph with a failure example is proposed (never written to the file here); declined = not worth a check (one-off, judgment call already covered, no evidence); blocked = could not finish (R9 pause, probe could not run, brain unreachable). Only blocked may be retried as is.

fingerprint.description: The candidate's stable id from collect_candidates.py: the drafted rule id, else a slug of the statement. Also the artifact's directory name.

band.description: The highest band of the fix ladder that can catch this mistake. structure = change the code or API so the mistake cannot be written; static = a lint, type or conventions rule; verification = the agent proves it by running the app; prose = a guidelines line, the last resort; none = declined or blocked before placement.

statement.description: The mistake and the right move, in one or two sentences.

refs.description: Where each occurrence was seen: <ticket>/review.json#findings[i], a fix_lessons id, a session id, <KEY>/prod-verify.json or eval:<case id>@<sha12> for a review miss.

why_not_higher.description: One entry for every band ABOVE `band` that was considered and rejected, with the reason. Empty only when band is structure (or none). This is the anti-prose guard: a guideline-proposed artifact must show why structure, static and verification could not catch it.

rule.description: band=static, conventions route: the exact rule object rule_probe.py proved (format: dev-pre-pr/references/violation-rules.md). Its `fix` is the message the next agent reads at the gate.

failures.description: Failure classes from rule_probe.py when it failed.

existing_copies.description: Inventory count: copies of the mistake already in the target repo.

ticket_draft.description: Path of the drafted ticket (issue_tracker ticket shape), for band=structure, a target linter rule, or the cleanup of existing copies. Drafted, never filed.

expectation.description: band=verification: the proposed expectation statement (proposed through qa-kb, never blessed here).

guideline.description: band=prose: the proposed guidelines paragraph, including one example of the failure.

miss.description: v1.1.0: present only when the correction is a review MISS (source `review-miss`): the review let through a bug that a prod run or the reviewer eval set later confirmed. collect_misses.py fills origin, ref, review_verdict, locations and had; dev-harden fills `lacked` before placing anything (DEV-HARDEN-M1).

origin.description: prod-regressed = infra-prod-verify said prod-regressed for the run; eval-missed = a bad reviewer-eval case where no confirmed bug was located; eval-partial = some but not all were located; human-reported = a person queued the miss by hand.

ref.description: <KEY>/prod-verify.json for a prod run; eval:<case id>@<first 12 hex of case_set.sha256> for an eval case.

review_verdict.description: What the reviewer answered (review.json `verdict`, or the eval case's verdict). null = no review ran, or it is unknown.

locations.description: The confirmed bug ranges the reviewer did not locate. Empty for a prod run until a human confirms one.

had.description: Mechanical facts of what was in front of the reviewer, copied from the queue entry: for a prod run reviewed, review_findings, masking, context_pack, brief_status, evidence; for an eval case masking, unmatched_findings, unlocatable_findings, case_set_sha256, score_status.

lacked.description: What the reviewer did not have in front of it. Judgment, so the collector leaves it null; dev-harden decides it from the evidence before placing the miss (DEV-HARDEN-M1).

kind.description: check = no rule, type or test existed that would have failed on the bug; context = the code it needed (a caller, a bypasser, a sibling path) was outside the diff and the context pack; expectation = the intended behaviour was written nowhere the reviewer reads; instruction = the guidelines, the review brief or the reviewer's own skill never told it to look; nothing = it had everything, a judgment slip no artifact would have changed (must end declined).

statement.description: One or two sentences: what was missing and where it should have been.

evidence.description: Optional: the file, finding or diff line that shows it.
